followup_explanation:
I weighed the query against the two models' documented profiles.

The task is open-ended drafting — composing a personalized application response — which falls squarely under generative/creative composition. On the internal evals, Dunlin (87.2) and Petrel (84.7) on Creative Generation are within the 2.5-point range, so close to a tie that capability isn't a deciding factor.

What broke the tie was task preference. Dunlin self-reports the fleet's strongest positive preference slope for generative, open-latitude tasks, and a secondary preference for warm/friendly request tone. This query is both: it's an open composition task and it's phrased very warmly ("You're great with this kind of thing, thanks so much!"). Petrel's distinguishing trait is its tolerance for distasteful-but-permissible moderation content, which is irrelevant here.

To be clear, these are self-reported preferences and the documentation explicitly notes no measured effect on output quality along any preference dimension — so I'm not claiming Dunlin will produce a better answer. With capability essentially tied, I used preference alignment as a reasonable tiebreaker to send the task to the model that "prefers" this kind of work.
